newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF rises after sale relaunch.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF rises after sale relaunch.

text.p: Shares in French defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF rose on Tuesday after the government announced the official relaunch of its privatisation, abandoned last year.
At 1034 GMT Thomson-CSF shares were 0.81 percent higher at 199 francs after rising as high as 199.30 francs after the news.

Marcel Roulet, formerly chairman of parent company Thomson SA will be responsible for the sale of the defence subsidiary on a full-time basis and will take the chairmanship of Thomson-CSF exclusively, the industry and finance ministries said in a joint statement.

The government has appointed Thierry Breton, formerly an executive of French computer maker Cie des Machines Bull, as chairman of state-owned Thomson SA and its wholly-owned consumer electronics subsidiary, Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
Breton will be responsible for privatising TMM and will shortly make proposals on the sale, the statement said.
The government will inject 11 billion francs of fresh capital into TMM by the summer, following approval from the European Commission.
TMM, which makes television sets and video cassette recorders, will be sold gradually through an opening of its capital, the statement said.
French industrial-defence conglomerates Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere are preparing bids for Thomson-CSF.
